decision: Close the one-thread child-panic regression BOUNDED_UNRESOLVED. Its R1 controller failure preceded every process; its R2 baseline build was fully supervised but the frozen source inventory omitted the README required by pinned src/main.rs. No control or candidate observation exists. Select SOURCE-LOCK-COMPLETENESS-AUDIT-1 READY and unstarted as the highest-value feasible local successor: it can statically characterize the source-lock boundary without inventing/fetching a byte. Pipeline completeness remains broader but is still blocked by its independent receipt-semantics protocol gate.

categories.assessment: The selected source-lock audit is a low-cost static provenance method directly motivated by the stopped item's exact build boundary. Pipeline completeness remains the broader discovery method but lacks its prerequisite protocol.

The stopped child-panic matrix remains unobserved. A static complete/missing dependency ledger can become a reusable source-materialization asset; pipeline completeness could later provide a checked-object sentinel after its own gate.
No current external defect or maintainer request follows from an incomplete local pin. The selected audit is local-only; pipeline completeness also needs no external action at this stage.
The selected audit reuses only local source, Cargo and closure evidence. Pipeline completeness requires an independent producer/adapter/receipt review before it can justify reuse.
The selected audit directly characterizes the frozen source-lock blocker without bypassing it. Pipeline completeness remains blocked by a scientific protocol gate rather than an external dependency.

candidates.rationale: Selected READY and unstarted. It has a fixed local source-only scope, eight-inspection cap and zero-process/network boundary. It can preserve the exact README omission and audit other locally visible compile-time path dependencies without changing the frozen failed run.
This keeps stronger broad transfer value but lacks a pinned producer/adapters, checked-object receipt semantics, independent expected contents and fixed fault rubric.

blockers.reason: Bind the supported producer and adapters, a twelve-declaration expectation, receipt semantics, fixed faults and finite source/setup/build/tooling/process controls before promotion.
